title: Physics-Guided Robotic Radiation Source Localization Along Arbitrary Measurement Paths in Unstructured Environments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
summary: A physics-informed ML model with attenuation-aware model tensors estimates the source location from arbitrary measurement paths among unknown obstacles. It is validated in Monte Carlo transport simulations and real-robot tests.
relation: Explicitly argues that approaching the source raises the risk of radiation damage to the robot and therefore decouples localization from path planning. This matches the thesis's motivation, but there is no budget, learned policy or exit reserve.

title: Localizing multiple radiation sources actively with a particle filter
summary: An autonomous mobile robot surveys a region with static obstacles along an information-driven (not pre-planned) trajectory. A regularized particle filter continuously estimates the number and parameters of the sources.
relation: The Lazna & Zalud particle-filter work: closest to the thesis's estimator (particle filter, obstacles, unknown intensity). It uses one robot and has no dose budget or exit reserve.

title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Radiation Localization
summary: Presents RAD-TEAM, an on-policy model-free policy-gradient MARL framework that extends Proctor et al.'s single-agent approach to any number of cooperating agents searching for a source of unknown location in obstructed environments.
relation: Closest prior multi-agent RL radiation search (same Portland State lineage as RAD-A2C). The abstract mentions no per-robot dose budget, safety layer or exit reserve, which is the gap the thesis targets.

title: Real-Time Avoidance of Ionising Radiation Using Layered Costmaps for Mobile Robots
summary: Adds a radiation layer to the ROS costmap (inverse-distance-weighted interpolation of observations) so planners avoid exposure. This cut accumulated dose to background levels in real deployment and by up to 10x in simulation.
relation: Minimizes the robot's cumulative dose, motivated by electronics lifetime. It is a soft cost with no hard budget, no exit reserve and no source search, but it is a key dose-aware navigation reference.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization for Radiation Source Search
summary: Investigates deep RL (PPO-trained actor-critic) for sequential source search with a single mobile detector under weak sources, background radiation and obstructions (non-convex environments); this is the RAD-A2C line of work, which other works describe as an actor-critic augmented with a particle filter embedded in the network.
relation: Main single-agent DRL baseline for the thesis (PPO, obstacles, unknown intensity), but it has no robot dose budget, no exit/return constraint and only one agent.

title: Robotic Exploration of an Unknown Nuclear Environment Using Radiation Informed Autonomous Navigation
summary: A UGV converts gamma measurements into its navigation stack so that it actively avoids high-dose regions while exploring and travelling between waypoints, to prevent robot breakdowns. It identified two sources in experiments.
relation: Motivates robot-dose limits: a broken-down robot fails the mission and can block access routes. It avoids dose heuristically, without a budget, exit reserve or uncertainty-aware prediction.

title: SACCL: A reinforcement learning-based approach for radiation source localization
summary: Soft Actor-Critic with curriculum learning, prioritized replay, selective state encoding and a radiation-aware adaptive speed. It reaches 93-100% success with and without obstacles and beats SAC, TD3, PF-PPO and Infotaxis baselines.
relation: Recent single-agent DRL baseline that uses PF-PPO and Infotaxis as comparators. Adapting speed to radiation intensity is a performance device, not a dose budget, and there is no exit reserve.

title: Autonomous Radiation Mapping Using a Manipulator-Equipped Quadruped with Flexible Behavior Design
summary: Spot quadruped with manipulator-held gamma spectrometer performs Bayesian-optimization adaptive mapping with a fault-tolerant behaviour tree, locating a Cs-137 source and its intensity in an obstacle-rich testbed.
relation: Single-robot active source localization in cluttered space; no robot dose constraint or team.

title: Physics-Guided Gaussian Process Mapping of Strong-Gradient Radiation Fields from Mobile Robot Surveys: The Role of Sampling Geometry
summary: Physics-guided GP reconstructs strong-gradient collimated Cs-137 fields from tracked-robot surveys; reliability depends on sampling geometry and extrapolation.
relation: Shows where radiation field models can be trusted from robot samples, relevant to model error and overconfidence.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Augmentation of Data Collection for Bayesian Optimization Towards Radiation Survey and Source Localization
summary: Adds an RL component to Bayesian-optimization radiation search so transit paths collect informative data; tested on three real radiation datasets, improving max-point score at ~2x compute.
relation: Learning-based radiation search precedent; single agent and no dose constraint on the robot.

title: Radiation Mapping: A Gaussian Multi-Kernel Weighting Method for Source Investigation in Disaster Scenarios
summary: Multi-kernel GPR with attenuation and energy-dependent kernels for radiation mapping in shielded environments; deployed on a mobile robot with NaI detector, 10-15 cm localization errors.
relation: Models shielding-induced field discrepancy, relevant to the thesis' correlated model error finding.

title: Automated Robotic Exploration of Noisy Radiation Fields from Raw Real-World Radiation Data using a Dynamically Enhanced Implementation of Bayesian Optimization
venue: Journal of Nuclear Engineering and Radiation Science
summary: Dynamic-measurement Bayesian optimization for robotic radiation field exploration on raw real-world data including a research reactor with attenuation obstacles.
relation: Radiation search with real attenuated fields; single agent, no dose budget.

title: Radiation Source Localization Considering Shielding Effect of Structures Using 3D Object Recognition
venue: IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration
summary: Uses 3D object recognition to identify shielding structures, corrects measured dose for their attenuation, and localizes sources via ML-EM in regions selected by an EKF.
relation: Addresses obstacle-induced model error in source estimation, relevant to the thesis' finding of filter overconfidence under spatially correlated model error.

title: Real-Time Radiological Source Term Estimation for Multiple Sources in Cluttered Environments
summary: A particle filter estimates the position, strength and number of sources in obstacle-rich areas, using precomputed attenuation kernels and dynamic particle allocation, with up to eight sources.
relation: Its attenuation-kernel precomputation applies directly to fast dose prediction behind obstacles in the thesis. Estimation only, with no dose-aware control.

title: An Autonomous Clutter Inspection Approach for Radiological Survey Using Mobile Robot
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
summary: Mobile robot clutter inspection using a particle filter to localize hotspots and estimate intensity, with worst-case analysis of detector limitations; real Geiger-Muller experiments.
relation: Particle-filter source estimation with worst-case reasoning, akin to the thesis' percentile-based safety.

title: Online 2D-3D Radiation Mapping and Source Localization using Gaussian Processes with Mobile Ground Robots
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security and Rescue Robotics
summary: Online 2D/3D GP radiation mapping and source localization on ground robots with uncertainty quantification, evaluated at EnRicH 2023.
relation: Uncertainty-aware field estimation alternative to the particle filter.

title: An autonomous radiation source detection policy based on deep reinforcement learning with generalized ability in unknown environments
summary: Splits detection into exploration and localization subtasks. Low-level DRL controllers carry out each subtask and a high-level controller chooses between them, which generalizes across geometries.
relation: Hierarchical DRL for single-robot search. Its option-switching resembles the thesis's 'withdraw' action, but it has no dose budget or exit constraint.

title: Optimization Strategies for Bayesian Source Localization Algorithms
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
summary: Compares existing and three new measurement-selection strategies for Bayesian radioactive source localization, aiming to minimize the number of measurements needed.
relation: Its active-sensing heuristics are candidate non-learned baselines. It considers no dose or exit.

title: A coverage path planning approach for autonomous radiation mapping with a mobile robot
venue: International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems
summary: Coverage path planner (sampling points, NN+DFS, K-means clustering) for autonomous radiation mapping with a Geiger-Muller-equipped mobile robot, validated in simulation and real experiments.
relation: Single-robot exhaustive mapping without source estimation or robot dose budget; a coverage baseline contrasting with the thesis's estimate-driven, dose-limited search.

title: Autonomous mapping and spectroscopic analysis of distributed radiation fields using aerial robots
summary: Online distributed gamma field estimation with isotope classification and an informative path planner for endurance-limited micro aerial robots in GPS-denied settings, with uranium/radium experiments.
relation: Source characterization under a limited endurance budget; budget is flight time, not dose.

title: A fast gamma-ray source localization method for mobile robots.
summary: Fast source parameter estimation with triangulation initialisation and hill-climbing MLE, tested with a NaI robot searching for Co-60.
relation: Single-robot Co-60 estimation; MLE rather than particle filter, no dose budget.

title: Investigating the Interpretability of ML-Guided Radiological Source Searches
summary: Augments an RL-based CNN radiological source search agent with feedback on search progress, termination confidence and projected actions.
relation: Single-detector RL source search; relevant for RL search and termination confidence.

title: Informative path planner with exploration-exploitation trade-off for radiological surveys in non-convex scenarios
summary: Informative path planner with B-spline paths maximizing a GP-based modified mutual information that rewards high-field regions; improves source position estimates in non-convex environments.
relation: Information-driven radiological survey that deliberately approaches sources, without accounting for robot dose; the thesis adds a dose budget against exactly this incentive.

title: Path Planning for Localization of Radiation Sources Based on Principal Component Analysis
summary: Path planning for a mobile robot with omnidirectional gamma imager: approach the source then encircle it using PCA of past measurements; validated in experiments.
relation: Single-robot active source localization without dose limits.

title: Autonomous Search of Radioactive Sources through Mobile Robots
summary: Frames source search as a POMDP with a Bayesian estimate of the source parameters and a reward-driven action set. It is validated on a TurtleBot with a 37 MBq Cs-137 source indoors.
relation: POMDP framing with a belief over the source, as in the thesis. It has one robot and no dose or exit constraints.

title: Mobile Robotic Radiation Surveying With Recursive Bayesian Estimation and Attenuation Modeling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
summary: Recursive Bayesian estimation (grid and particle filter) with environmental attenuation models, isotope identification and Fisher-information-optimized survey points, demonstrated on two mobile robots without operator intervention.
relation: Its goal is to remove human operator dose. The robot's own dose is not budgeted and it has no exit reserve.

title: Informative Mobile Robot Exploration for Radiation Source Localization with a Particle Filter
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotic Computing (IRC)
summary: Localizes an unknown source under measurement uncertainty using a particle filter with information-gain-based exploration, as an alternative to gradient descent.
relation: Single-robot particle-filter plus information-gain pipeline similar to the thesis's estimator. It has no dose budget.

title: Localization of Ionizing Radiation Sources by Cooperating Micro Aerial Vehicles With Pixel Detectors in Real-Time
summary: Releases an open-source Gazebo/ROS plugin that simulates Timepix detectors and sources (ray-tracing plus Monte Carlo, including obstacles) and demonstrates cooperative source localization by a group of MAVs.
relation: Useful simulation tooling and a cooperative-localization reference. It has no dose budgets.

title: Double Q-Learning for Radiation Source Detection
summary: A CNN-based double Q-learning agent navigates a detector in a simulated radiation environment. It cuts search time by at least 44% compared with uniform and gradient search.
relation: Early DRL source search with one detector. It optimizes search time only and considers neither the robot's dose nor safe exit.

title: Experiments in unmanned aerial vehicle/unmanned ground vehicle radiation search
summary: In field tests at Savannah River, a UAV and a UGV fuse aerial and ground spectra. A point-source model with information-theoretic active exploration lets the UGV locate material online.
relation: Information-theoretic active search on real robots. It has no dose budget or exit.

title: Bayesian Metropolis methods for source localization in an urban environment
summary: Metropolis MCMC estimation of gamma source location and intensity from a detector network, incorporating uncertain building cross sections into the posterior.
relation: Relates to model-error-aware posteriors; the thesis finds PF overconfident under correlated model error.

title: Autonomous Exploration for Radioactive Hotspots Localization Taking Account of Sensor Limitations
summary: Behaviour-based and MCDM exploration strategies for radioactive hotspot localization accounting for gamma camera acquisition time and angular resolution, validated on a real robot.
relation: Single-robot radiation search; no dose budget on robot.

title: Cooperation between an unmanned aerial vehicle and an unmanned ground vehicle in highly accurate localization of gamma radiation hotspots
venue: International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems
summary: A UAV builds an orthophoto and terrain map (and rough radiation map). A UGV with sensitive probes, including a differential dual-probe setup, then follows optimized trajectories to localize hotspots precisely.
relation: Heterogeneous UAV/UGV field system. Coordination is operator-in-the-loop rather than learned, and it has no dose budgeting.

title: Radiation Source Localization in GPS-Denied Environments Using Aerial Robots
summary: An aerial robot with a CsI(Tl)/SiPM detector and visual-inertial localization runs active source search path planning. The planning accounts for limited flight endurance (few dwell points) and uncertainty in the robot's pose.
relation: Plans search under a non-renewable resource budget (battery endurance), a close analogue to the thesis's dose budget, though the robot's own dose is not modelled.

title: Information driven search for point sources of gamma radiation
summary: A sequential Bayesian estimator (Poisson counts, inverse-square model) estimates the number, locations and strengths of sources, and a controller moves the observer(s) to maximize Renyi-divergence information gain. It is validated on field-trial data.
relation: Seminal information-driven radiation search that jointly estimates position and activity, as the thesis's particle filter does. Low-level sources, so no robot dose or exit considerations.

title: A controlled search for radioactive point sources
summary: In a polygonal area with obstacles, a particle filter detects and estimates an unknown number of sources, and a group of networked Geiger-counter observers is steered by Renyi-divergence information gain.
relation: Early multi-observer, obstacle-aware information-driven search with a particle filter. It has no dose budget or exit reserve.

title: Information driven localisation of a radiological point source
summary: Joint detection and estimation of a point source's location and intensity with a particle filter. Observer motion and exposure time are chosen by multi-step-ahead maximization of Fisher information gain.
relation: Its stated aim of cutting observation time, and with it radiation exposure, is an early exposure-aware motivation. It sets no explicit budget, has no exit and uses one observer.

title: Operational verification of a hexapod-robot system equipped with a Compton camera for visualizing radiation sources while overcoming obstacles
summary: Hexapod robot guided by Compton camera direction estimates moves toward a Cs-137 source, overcoming pipes, boards and stairs.
relation: Direction-guided single-robot source approach; ignores robot dose and multi-robot coordination.

title: Development of optimization-based algorithms for radiation source localization in nuclear emergencies
venue: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
summary: Title only: optimization-based algorithms for radiation source localization in nuclear emergencies.
relation: Source estimation methods; exposure-constraint aspects unknown.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Path Planning for Radioactive Source Search
summary: Proposes a DRL-based path planning strategy for autonomous radioactive source search by robots in nuclear decommissioning.
relation: Single-robot DRL search motivated by worker risk. The truncated abstract does not show any robot dose budget or exit constraint.

title: Physics-informed radiation multi-source localization with robotic platform
venue: International Journal of Intelligent Robotics and Applications
summary: A source-count classifier trained on about 60k simulated flux samples, combined with physics-informed neural networks, localizes an unknown number of sources from sparse measurements along a predefined robot path.
relation: Physics-informed localization. The path is predefined (no active control) and the robot's dose is not handled.

title: Identification of Unknown Multiple Radiation Sources Using Change Rate of Gamma Rays with Directional Detector
summary: Exploration path generation to localize multiple radiation sources of unknown intensity using the rate of change of gamma counts with a directional detector.
relation: Single-robot source localization method; no dose constraint.

title: A Rapid Reconstruction Method of Gamma Radiation Field Based on Normalized Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
summary: Robot-assisted gamma field mapping coupling normalized POD with minimax adaptive selection of measurement locations; uncertainty-aware weighted least squares reduces error in a 2-D experiment.
relation: Field reconstruction from sparse robot stops; offers a model-reduction alternative to the thesis's point-source particle filter but ignores robot exposure.

title: A Behavioral Robotics Approach to Radiation Mapping Using Adaptive Sampling
summary: Quadruped robot with manipulator and gamma detector selects measurement points by surrogate-model uncertainty (Bayesian optimization), adapting exploration after collisions; tested with Cs-137.
relation: Uncertainty-driven single-robot radiation mapping; no robot dose accounting or multi-agent coordination.

title: A radioactive source-seeking method based on angle constraint and particle diffusion
summary: A particle-filter-based mobile robot search method that uses an angle constraint to cut complexity and particle diffusion to keep estimates accurate in unknown environments.
relation: Single-robot particle-filter source seeking. It has no dose or exit constraints.

title: A direction-aimed radiation detector and strength estimation method based on mobile robot system
venue: International Symposium on Sensors, Mechatronics, and Automation
summary: Vehicle-mounted directional detector (0.15 uGy/h to 500 Gy/h range) with conjugate-Gamma Bayesian strength estimation applied to a real radiation source search task.
relation: Bayesian source-strength estimation on a mobile robot for high-dose-rate fields; single robot, no dose constraint.

title: 3D Radiation Mapping Using Gaussian Process Regression with Intensity Projection
summary: GP regression with an inverse-square-law-inspired kernel builds 3D radiation maps from mobile-robot data and estimates sources.
relation: Physics-informed field model; complements the thesis's parametric particle filter.

title: A study of robotic search strategy for multi-radiation sources in unknown environments
summary: Robotic search for multiple sources in unknown environments. OpenAlex keywords indicate receding-horizon planning, a particle filter, adaptive differential evolution and an exploration-exploitation balance (no abstract available).
relation: Single-robot multi-source planner. No dose budget is indicated.

title: Autonomous exploration for radioactive sources localization based on radiation field reconstruction
summary: A UGV iterates path planning, Gaussian-process reconstruction of the radiation field and peak analysis to localize sources, with about 0.30 m error on a real Cs-137 source.
relation: Uses a map-based (GPR) estimate instead of a parametric particle filter. One robot, no dose budget.

title: Heuristic techniques for maximum likelihood localization of radioactive sources via a sensor network
summary: Heuristic optimisation to speed MLE estimation of radioactive source parameters with a sensor network.
relation: Static sensor network estimation, not mobile robots.

title: Localizing unknown radiation sources by unscented particle filtering based on divide-and-conquer sampling
venue: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology
summary: An unscented particle filter with divide-and-conquer sampling counters particle degeneracy and impoverishment when mobile robots search for unknown sources.
relation: Offers particle-filter refinements that could make the thesis's shared estimator and its quantile estimates more robust.

title: Rapid localization of radioactive leaks based on hybrid adaptive grey wolf algorithm
summary: Hybrid adaptive grey wolf optimizer localizes single and double radioactive leak points from exposure-rate changes, with attenuation and scattering modelled.
relation: Optimization-based localization alternative to particle filtering; no robot dose or multi-agent aspect.

title: An Alpha/Beta Radiation Mapping Method Using Simultaneous Localization and Mapping for Nuclear Power Plants
summary: Autonomous alpha/beta radiation mapping framework projecting detector readings onto a LiDAR SLAM map, tested in ROS indoors and outdoors.
relation: Mapping rather than source estimation; no exposure constraint.

title: Radioactive source search problem and optimisation model based on meta-heuristic algorithm
summary: Meta-heuristic search algorithm imitating technicians to locate lost radioactive sources, with linear complexity and good efficiency in simulation.
relation: Single-searcher heuristic search; no dose budget or team.

title: Gamma Radiation Source Localization for Micro Aerial Vehicles with a Miniature Single-Detector Compton Event Camera
venue: International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (ICUAS)
summary: A 40 g single-detector Compton camera (MiniPIX TPX3 CdTe) on a micro aerial vehicle reconstructs directions to the source and fuses them onboard in real time to localize a Cs-137 source.
relation: Directional (Compton) sensing on a robot localizes the source without approaching it, an alternative way to limit exposure. Not dose-budgeted.

title: State-of-the-Art Mobile Radiation Detection Systems for Different Scenarios
summary: Reviews post-Fukushima mobile gamma and neutron detection systems, platforms (especially UAVs) and cooperative search across accident, illicit-trafficking, facility and NORM scenarios.
relation: Background review for detector and platform choices. It does not address dose-budgeted planning.

title: A Bayesian method to localize lost gamma sources
summary: A feasibility study of Bayesian estimation of orphan-source position and activity from vehicle-mounted HPGe mobile gamma spectrometry, tested with Cs-137, Ba-133 and I-131.
relation: Supports joint position and activity estimation, which matters because the thesis's dose predictions depend on the uncertain activity. There is no control.

title: Active Range and Bearing-based Radiation Source Localization
venue: IEEE/RJS International Conference on Intelligent RObots and Systems
summary: Gamma-camera mapping plus greedy Fisher-information waypoint selection with adaptive step size for 3D source localization.
relation: Information-driven single-robot search; no dose budget.

title: Use of Multi-Rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for Radioactive Source Search
summary: Low-cost multi-rotor UAV platform with three search algorithms; field tests located a radioactive source with 0.32 m error.
relation: Aerial source search precedent; single vehicle, low-activity sources, no dose constraint.

title: Radiation search operations using scene understanding with autonomous UAV and UGV
summary: Aerial imagery provides an orthophoto, a DEM and semantic segmentation that identify radiological points of interest. A UGV with LiDAR and a detector then plans paths to collect more precise ground measurements.
relation: Heterogeneous field system for radiation search. Planning is not learned and there is no dose budget.

title: Hybrid optimization and Bayesian inference techniques for a non‐smooth radiation detection problem
summary: Hybrid global/local optimization and adaptive MCMC to estimate radiation source location and intensity in an urban block with non-smooth likelihood.
relation: Source estimation alternatives to particle filtering with uncertainty quantification.

title: UAV-based multiple source localization and contour mapping of radiation fields
summary: UAV approach for localizing multiple radiation sources and contour mapping, handling scattered, clustered and biased source distributions.
relation: Aerial multi-source localization; no robot exposure constraint.

title: Search strategy of a mobile robot for radiation sources in an unknown environment
venue: International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
summary: A search strategy that lets a mobile robot find radiation sources autonomously in an unknown environment without a prior map.
relation: Early single-robot autonomous search. Its abstract frames robot exposure as harmless, the opposite of the thesis's assumption.

title: Mobile Sensor Network Control Using Mutual Information Methods and Particle Filters
summary: Distributed information-theoretic control of mobile sensors that maximizes mutual information computed from a particle-filter posterior, with single-node and pairwise approximations to scale with team size.
relation: Methodological basis for a shared particle filter with information-seeking team motion. It is not radiation-specific and has no dose constraints.

title: Detection and parameter estimation of multiple radioactive sources
summary: Bayesian detection and parameter estimation for multiple radioactive point sources (summary based on title; cited as foundational by Proctor et al. 2021).
relation: Background on multi-source estimation. The thesis assumes a single source.

title: 'Infotaxis' as a strategy for searching without gradients
summary: Introduces infotaxis, a search strategy that moves to maximize the expected reduction in entropy of the source-location posterior when sparse cues make gradients unavailable.
relation: Basis of the entropy-reduction baselines and reward terms used in radiation search. It has no hazard or budget model.

title: Experimental implementation of robotic sequential nuclear search
venue: Mediterranean Conference on Control and Automation (MED)
summary: A hardware 'model-driven measurement' loop in which a physical-process model guides where the robot measures and the measurements update the model. It confirms weak sources at a set statistical confidence.
relation: Early robotic active nuclear search. It targets weak sources and does not consider the robot's own dose.

title: Heterogeneity: A multi-robot radioactive source search technique
summary: Multi-robot radioactive source search exploiting robot heterogeneity; OpenAlex keywords include particle filter, path planning and radioresistance (no abstract returned).
relation: Most relevant for unequal radiation tolerance across robots; rule/planner based, not learned, and (from available metadata) no explicit cumulative dose budget with guaranteed exit.

title: PSOPF-MATD3: A multi-agent collaborative radioactive source search strategy
summary: Combines a particle-swarm-optimized particle filter (shared source estimate) with multi-agent TD3 so agents learn collaborative search and collision avoidance.
relation: Very close architecture (shared PF + MARL policy); uses off-policy MATD3 rather than MAPPO and does not impose per-robot dose budgets, exit reserve or uncertainty-aware masking.

title: Leveraging Swarm Robotics for Environmental Radiation Monitoring: An Interdisciplinary Perspective
venue: 2025 9th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
summary: Integrates dynamic radiation source behaviour into a robot simulator to study swarms exploring and mapping radioactive environments, evaluating number of robots, their radiation tolerance and navigation efficiency.
relation: Close setting (multi-robot radiation exploration with robot radiation tolerance as a factor) but no learned policy, budget-aware withdrawal or estimate-dependent safety.

title: A heterogeneous robot collaborative search method for radioactive sources
summary: Cooperative search for radioactive sources by heterogeneous robot teams for nuclear emergency response, with planning formulated on Riemannian manifolds (keywords; no abstract returned).
relation: Same group as 'Heterogeneity'; heterogeneous team coordination is hand-designed, not MARL, and dose budgets/exit are not reported in metadata.

title: Multi-robot cooperative search for radioactive sources based on particle swarm optimization particle filter
summary: Each robot is a mobile observation platform whose latest observations are fused into particle sampling, while PSO moves particles toward high-likelihood regions to fight degeneracy.
relation: Provides the PSOPF estimator family the thesis can use as its shared filter; motion is heuristic and dose accumulation of robots is not constrained.

title: A proposal on multi-agent static path planning strategy for minimizing radiation dose
summary: Conflict-based search multi-agent path finding whose objective minimizes cumulative radiation dose, e.g., for evacuating many workers after an NPP accident.
relation: Directly multi-agent + cumulative dose (and evacuation/exit), but static known field and no source search or learning; dose minimized, not budgeted per agent.

title: Multi-robot collaborative radioactive source search based on particle fusion and adaptive step size
summary: Multi-robot collaborative search fusing particles from robots' detectors with an adaptive step-size motion rule (keywords; no abstract returned).
relation: Early key paper of the SWUST line; rule-based cooperative movement with shared estimate but no per-robot dose budget or withdrawal logic.

title: Target localization using Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Proximal Policy Optimization
summary: Multi-agent deep RL with PPO for cooperative target (radiation) localization by mobile sensing agents in environments with walls.
relation: Key MARL-PPO precedent (close to MAPPO); reward is localization performance, no agent exposure budget or safe exit.

title: Distributed Active Sensing for Multi-Robot Radiation Source Localization via Spatial-Probabilistic Decoupling
summary: Preprint on distributed active sensing for multi-robot radiation localization using Voronoi partitioning, particle filter and mutual information, addressing masking/range ambiguity (keywords).
relation: Information-theoretic planner, not RL; recent competitor for estimator-driven coordination without dose budgets.

title: An Intelligent Multi-Robot Mobile Measurement System for Active Cooperative Radiation Source Localization via Dynamic Voronoi Partitioning
summary: Preprint describing a multi-robot mobile measurement system with dynamic Voronoi partitioning, epistemic uncertainty handling and false-alarm filtering (keywords).
relation: Uncertainty-aware but rule-based; no cumulative dose accounting.

title: Multi-robot Collaborative Source Searching Method Based on Information Exploration and Exploitation
summary: Conference paper on multi-robot radioactive source search balancing information exploration and exploitation (title only returned).
relation: Information-driven heuristic baseline from the SWUST group; dose-agnostic.

title: Multi-robot autonomous search for radioactive leakage source based on a CPE-Infotaxis method during nuclear emergency rescue
summary: Distributed multi-robot Infotaxis where each robot weights received information by relative-entropy credibility, robust to radiation-induced sensor failures; ~40% faster than Infotaxis.
relation: Explicitly motivated by radiation damage to robots (sensor faults) but handles it via belief robustness, not dose budgets or exit reserve.

title: RADRON: Cooperative Localization of Ionizing Radiation Sources by MAVs With Compton Cameras
summary: Cooperating MAVs fuse single-detector Compton camera measurements to estimate radioactive source position.
relation: State-of-the-art cooperative aerial localization; exposure of agents not modeled.

title: HAMSAR: A Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-UAV Framework for Radiation Source Search in Unknown Environments With Multihop Communication and Auction-Based Task Allocation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
summary: Hierarchical multi-UAV framework using online radiation intensity cues, multihop communication and auction-based allocation for discovering multiple sources in unknown environments.
relation: Explicit allocation/exploration architecture; no per-agent dose budget.

title: Radiation source estimation using a connectivity-aware decentralized multi-mobile sensor system
summary: Decentralized mobile agents estimate an unknown source with a particle filter, keep communication connectivity via graph Laplacian estimates and plan with Shannon entropy; success rate rises to 94%.
relation: Adds communication constraints to multi-agent PF search; constraints are on connectivity, not cumulative dose.

title: Radiation source multi-agent search by drones
summary: Group of UAVs with short-range GM detectors exchange measurements and use particle fusion to improve search efficiency and source estimate accuracy.
relation: Multi-drone PF search (coauthor of Ling 2022); dose-agnostic.

title: Radioactive sources search method based on multi-robot and Voronoi partition
summary: Multi-robot radioactive source search partitioning the area by Voronoi cells with particle-filter estimation (keywords; no abstract returned).
relation: Spatial task allocation alternative to learned coordination; no per-robot dose constraint.

title: Adaptive target localization under uncertainty using Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with knowledge transfer
summary: MADRL localization that handles practical uncertainties such as false alarms when the target is absent or unreachable, using knowledge transfer.
relation: Deals with task uncertainty and termination, related to the thesis's withdraw action, but not agent dose safety.

title: Autonomous localization of multiple ionizing radiation sources using miniature single-layer Compton cameras onboard a group of micro aerial vehicles
summary: Group of MAVs with 44 g Compton cameras fuse distributed measurements to localize multiple gamma sources.
relation: Directional sensing in a team; no dose budget.

title: Enhancing radioactive environment exploration with bio-inspired swarm robotics: A comparative analysis of Lévy flight and stigmergy methods
summary: Compares Lévy flight and stigmergy swarm strategies for exploring radioactive environments.
relation: Swarm-level heuristic exploration; robots' dose not budgeted.

title: Distributed collaboration: Cognitive difference and collaborative decision for multi-robot radioactive source search
summary: Distributed multi-robot source search handling differences in robots' beliefs (cognitive difference) with a collaborative decision rule/reward function to reduce search time (keywords).
relation: Relevant to shared vs. local estimate design; optimizes search time, not radiation exposure of robots.

title: Multi-robot Cooperative Search for Radioactive Sources Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization
summary: Improved-PSO multi-robot search that fuses latest observations into particle sampling to mitigate particle degradation.
relation: Conference precursor of PSOPF; heuristic, dose-agnostic.

title: Multiagent Deep Reinforcement Learning With Demonstration Cloning for Target Localization
summary: Extends MADRL target localization by cloning demonstrations to speed up learning in environments with obstacles such as walls.
relation: Training-efficiency technique for MARL search; no safety/dose constraint.

title: Sequential Deployment of Mobile Radiation Sensor Network Using Reinforcement Learning in Radioactive Source Search
summary: RL to sequentially deploy a mobile radiation sensor network under physical and financial constraints for urban source search.
relation: Learned placement of a detector network; constraints are resource-based, not cumulative dose per robot.

title: An automated heterogeneous robotic system for radiation surveys: Design and field testing
summary: Multirobot (UAV+UGV) system for highly automated radiation surveys, replacing human operators in radiation-exposure missions; field tested.
relation: Real-world heterogeneous team reference; scripted mission roles, no learned policy or dose budget.

title: Using an Automated Heterogeneous Robotic System for Radiation Surveys
summary: Three-phase UAS then UGV system for aerial and terrestrial radiation mapping and source localization, validated in a staged field exercise.
relation: Multi-robot radiation search precedent, but sequential heterogeneous deployment without dose budgets or learned coordination.

title: Search and Localization of a Weak Source with a Multi-robot Formation
summary: Multi-robot formation search combining correlated random walk exploration and formation-based gradient estimation for a weak signal source under communication constraints (keywords).
relation: Formation-based search baseline; targets weak sources (thesis has strong source where dose matters).

title: Towards Expendable Robot Teaming in Extreme Environments
venue: International Journal of Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research
summary: Introduces 'expendable robot teaming' for nuclear waste management and decommissioning, where robots can be sacrificed under extreme hazards.
relation: Conceptual counterpoint to the thesis's per-robot dose budget and risk sharing (expendable vs. preserved robots).

title: Identification of low-level point radioactive sources using a sensor network
summary: Journal version extending triangulation to N-sensor localization of position and strength, then SPRT detection.
relation: Static network; no mobility or dose.

title: Identification of Low-Level Point Radiation Sources Using a Sensor Network
summary: Network of radiation sensors estimates location and strength of low-level point sources by geometric triangulation followed by sequential probability ratio test.
relation: Static detector network baseline for joint position+strength estimation (thesis estimates position and activity).

title: Distributed Decision Making for Electromagnetic Radiation Source Localization Using Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: MURPPO: distributed PPO with independent decisions and collaborative positioning by multiple UAVs to localize electromagnetic emitters in urban areas.
relation: Analogous MARL source localization (RF, not ionizing); no exposure budget.

title: A high-effective swarm intelligence-based multi-robot cooperation method for target searching in unknown hazardous environments
summary: Title only: swarm-intelligence-based multi-robot cooperation for target searching in unknown hazardous environments.
relation: Multi-robot hazardous search; whether exposure is constrained is unknown.

title: Multi-Robot Radiation Reconnaissance in the Chornobyl NPP Exclusion Zone
summary: Robotic radiation reconnaissance system of three robot types (UGV carrier and others) for mapping in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone.
relation: Applied heterogeneous team in real high-radiation area; no learned control or dose budgeting.

title: Radiation Surveys in Active Nuclear Facilities with Heterogeneous Collaborative Mobile Robots
summary: Robot Radiation Survey System with heterogeneous collaborating mobile robots for routine contamination surveys in active nuclear facilities.
relation: Practical multi-robot nuclear deployment; focus on contamination survey, not dose-budgeted search.

title: Machine learning for localization of radioactive sources via a distributed sensor network
summary: Supervised ML with feature extraction to detect and localize radioactive sources from a distributed sensor network.
relation: Learning-based static network localization; no mobility or dose.

title: Localization of a radioactive source in an urban environment using Bayesian Metropolis methods
venue: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A
summary: Bayesian MCMC estimation of gamma source location and intensity from a distributed detector network in an urban environment.
relation: Posterior over source position and intensity, analogous to the thesis's PF estimate; static sensors.

title: Nuclear threat detection with mobile distributed sensor networks
summary: Multiple vehicle-mounted detectors with known real-time positions are used to detect nuclear threats in urban areas.
relation: Mobile network detection background; agents not controlled for exposure.

title: Smart radiation sensor management
summary: Model-driven Bayesian radiation mapping strategies implemented on mobile robots for nuclear search and mapping.
relation: Early foundational work on robot-based radiation search; pre-2010 background.

title: Radioactive source detection by sensor networks
summary: Bayesian characterization of detection limits for networks detecting moving radioactive sources.
relation: Pre-2010 classic background on detector networks.

title: Robotics in Ionizing Radiation Environments: Vulnerabilities, Hardening, and Future Directions
summary: Reviews TID, displacement damage and single-event effects on robot electronics, sensing, actuation, power and communications, plus hardening, shielding and fault-tolerant architectures; notes a gap in linking component degradation to mission performance.
relation: Up-to-date review to cite for robot radiation vulnerability; its identified gap (component degradation to mission performance) motivates a mission-level dose budget.

title: Radiation Aware Navigation and Planning for Mobile Robot Exploration of Unknown Hazardous Nuclear Environments
summary: Thesis: sparse map abstraction plus hazard-weighted A* (85.6% lower cumulative dose for 17.2% longer paths) and online GPR radiation estimation for exploration (>75% lower dose), deployed on a Unitree Go2.
relation: Very recent robot-dose-minimising exploration framework; minimises dose but does not appear (from abstract) to enforce a hard budget with return.

title: Development and Deployment of Radiation-Tolerant Remotely-Control System in Fukushima Daiichi NPS
summary: For a sandbag-accumulation robot working for months in the Fukushima basement, radiation tolerance of electronics determined lifespan; the highly integrated PLC failed early, so it was moved to a low-dose area with remote I/O on the robot, extending lifespan 1.8x.
relation: Directly treats robot lifetime as limited by cumulative dose; supports modelling dose as a consumable, non-renewable resource.

title: Research on Radiation Damage and Reinforcement of Control and Sensing Systems in Nuclear Robots
summary: Irradiation of nuclear-robot components: Hall, pressure and temperature sensors damaged above 1300 Gy; transformers and controllers damaged above 170 Gy; Pb/W shielding (15 mm) improves controller protection.
relation: Component failure-dose thresholds; controllers (~170 Gy) are the weak link.

title: Multi-objective path planning for mobile robot in nuclear accident environment based on improved ant colony optimization with modified A*
summary: IACO-A* minimises path length, cumulative radiation dose and energy for a mobile robot on a Monte Carlo cost map, plus a high-dose-rate avoidance strategy triggered when lethal dose rates are sensed.
relation: Robot cumulative dose as a planning objective with a dose-rate-threshold avoidance rule (closest to a safety layer, but not a cumulative budget).

title: Radiation Field Detection of Nuclear Emergency Robot with Gamma Camera
venue: 2022 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM)
summary: Detection-pose planning for a nuclear emergency robot with a gamma camera using Fisher information, with a path planner that accounts for dose accumulation on the robot for unknown sources.
relation: Close single-robot precedent combining active source detection with robot dose accumulation; lacks a hard budget, exit reserve and team.

title: Radiation tolerance of a small COTS single board computer for mobile robots
summary: Co-60 irradiation of the UP Core single-board computer running ROS: units failed on average after 111.1 +/- 5.5 Gy, due to on-board power-management faults.
relation: Concrete failure-dose number for a typical mobile-robot computer; anchors the 0.1 Gy operating budget as a conservative fraction of COTS failure dose.

title: RICA: A Tracked Robot for Sampling and Radiological Characterization in the Nuclear Field
summary: CEA tracked robot that locates and measures radioactive sources; gamma irradiation tests gave component failure doses (some cards >1000 Gy, power supplies ~100 Gy, others >200 Gy). Full text (Scholar Gateway): 'the cumulative dose absorbed by the robot can be followed by dosimetry, as is done for human operators ... the robot's operating time in nominal conditions depends on the maximum dose acceptable for its weakest components.'
relation: Direct operational precedent for treating a robot's cumulative dose like a personal dose budget; used for maintenance scheduling, not for online planning with an exit reserve.

title: gamma Ray irradiation test of control system of nuclear emergency rescue robot
summary: Gamma irradiation of a nuclear emergency rescue robot control system: control system and communication link survived 100 Gy; an additional 300 Gy test identified the incapacitating total dose.
relation: System-level robot failure-dose data (~100+ Gy) for an emergency robot.

title: Emergency response to the nuclear accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plants using mobile rescue robots
summary: Describes retrofitting the Quince rescue robot for Fukushima Daiichi; gamma irradiation tests at JAEA showed the commercial electronics operated more than 100 h at a 10% safety margin in an assumed 100 mGy/h field, i.e. on the order of 10 Gy+ cumulative dose.
relation: Canonical example of sizing a robot's mission by its tolerable cumulative dose in a known dose-rate field; supports the dose-budget framing.

title: Extreme Total Ionizing Dose Survival of a COTS Artix-7 FPGA Under Prolonged Gamma Irradiation
venue: International Conference on Automation and Computing (ICAC)
summary: A continuously powered Artix-7 FPGA board accumulated ~6,680 Gy over 93.6 h; FPGA fabric survived but the QSPI flash failed, preventing autonomous reconfiguration.
relation: Shows peripherals (flash) set the effective failure dose; wide spread of tolerances across components.

title: Radiation-Aware Path Planning Framework for Mobile Robots in Dynamic Hazardous Environments
summary: A* + chaotic PSO + B-spline smoothing with exposure-dependent speed adaptation on a mSv/h dose-rate map with shielding attenuation; 21-47% lower cumulative absorbed dose than A*.
relation: Recent robot dose-aware planner with attenuation-aware field model.

title: Indoor UAV for Nuclear Investigation: Experimental Qualification and Field Feedback
summary: Field report of an indoor UAV at CEA Marcoule; located a Cs-137 source in blind tests and notes commercial electronics require conservative cumulative-dose management and short battery life.
relation: Practitioner evidence that cumulative dose to robot electronics is a real operational constraint, supporting the dose-budget premise.

title: From Single Platforms Towards Coordinated Fleets: Safety- and Security-Bounded Autonomous Multi-Robot Systems for Nuclear Decommissioning in Europe
summary: XS-ABILITY: heterogeneous legged/wheeled/aerial robot fleet for radiological characterisation with energy-aware task allocation, risk-aware navigation and a supervisory safety controller; field test of a single platform (TRL 4-5).
relation: Real-world multi-robot nuclear system design; radiation endurance and fleet coordination not evaluated, which the thesis addresses in simulation.

title: RI-RRT*: a riemannian metric-based path planning algorithm for autonomous robots in nuclear environments
venue: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology
summary: RI-RRT* embeds radiation intensity and obstacles into a Riemannian metric to plan low cumulative-dose paths; Geant4 simulations show 3-12% dose reduction, validated on a UAV.
relation: Cumulative-dose-aware planning in a known field; thesis plans under an uncertain field and a hard budget.

title: Design, protection, perception and planning of mobile robots in nuclear power plants
summary: Large review (300+ refs) of mobile robots in NPPs covering design, radiation protection/shielding, perception, path planning, source localization and multi-robot collaboration.
relation: Recent comprehensive review spanning robot protection and dose-aware planning.

title: Research on key technology and application progress of rescue robot in nuclear accident emergency situation
summary: Reviews nuclear-accident emergency rescue robots (reconnaissance, radiation monitoring, decontamination, communication) and proposes key technical parameters.
relation: Background on emergency-response robot requirements including radiation resistance.

title: A Dynamic Nuclear Radiation Environment Path Planning Method Based on an Improved Ant Colony Algorithm
summary: Dijkstra-improved ACO for minimum cumulative-dose robot paths in dynamically changing radiation fields during emergencies; ~21% lower cumulative dose than ACO.
relation: Robot cumulative-dose minimisation in nuclear emergencies.

title: A Real-Time Path Planning Algorithm in Radiation Environments Based on an Improved A* Combined with the Dynamic Window Approach
summary: Combines improved A* (length, cumulative dose, energy) with a radiation-aware DWA to mitigate radiation damage to onboard components under highly uncertain fields; ~23% lower cumulative dose.
relation: Explicitly motivated by onboard component damage and uncertain fields; soft-cost approach.

title: Design and Implementation of the Scenario Simulation System for Robotic Operations in Nuclear Radiation Environment
venue: 2025 IEEE 26th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Applications (CCSSTA)
summary: Unity3D simulator integrating SuperMC radiation fields to plan robot paths and compute real-time accumulated dose on sensitive electronic components.
relation: Evaluates robot cumulative dose for a known field offline; the thesis handles an unknown source with online budgeted control.

title: Multi-Objective Path Planning of Robots in Nuclear Environments Based on Improved Ant Colony Algorithm
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Control (ICRAIC)
summary: Hybrid A*-directed ant colony optimization path planner jointly minimizing path length, accumulated radiation dose and energy, validated in simulation and a robot experiment in a radiation field.
relation: Dose-aware planning with a known radiation field; the thesis must plan dose under an uncertain, estimated field and a hard budget.

title: A Path Planning Algorithm Considering the Feasibility Region of Nuclear Decommissioning Robots
summary: Proposes a dynamic-constraint A* (DC-A*) planner for nuclear decommissioning robots that accounts for robot footprint and orientation in narrow passages while avoiding radiation sources. Experiments show reduced dose accumulation and higher task success.
relation: Dose-minimizing planning with a known field for a single robot; the thesis instead budgets dose under an uncertain source estimate during search.

title: Assessment of Radiation Tolerance of Flash Memory by gamma-Ray Irradiation
summary: Gamma tests of a Raspberry Pi for decommissioning robots found its boot flash memory had particularly low radiation tolerance, limiting operating duration; some high-performance flash memories were more tolerant.
relation: Another COTS computer whose weakest component limits dose lifetime.

title: Irradiation of Commercial Equipment for Robotic Applications in a Highly Ionizing Radiation Field
summary: Evaluates commercial equipment for robotic platforms in high-radiation fields at various dose rates and determines TID for catastrophic failure for some items (values not stated in abstract).
relation: Additional COTS failure-dose source to check in full text.

title: Multi-objective path planning for mobile robots in nuclear radiation environment
summary: Improved ACO-A* multi-objective path planner minimising path length, cumulative radiation dose and energy for a mobile robot in a radiation field.
relation: Dose-aware planning in a known field; thesis faces an unknown source and a hard budget.

title: The effect of ionizing radiation on robotic trajectory movement and electronic components
summary: Irradiates microcontrollers, servo motors and temperature sensors at 0.09-1.5 Gy/s and a 3-DoF arm, comparing rad-hard MCUs and shielding as mitigation to extend operational lifespan.
relation: Component-level dose effects on robot motion; supports lifetime-limited-by-dose assumption.

title: The search for orphan radioactive source based on GPR-PRM method
summary: Orphan-source localization by alternating GPR radiation-field reconstruction and PRM/improved-A* path planning for a mobile robot, in simulated rooms with shielding.
relation: Orphan-source recovery with a mobile robot (no robot dose constraint).

title: CARMA II: A ground vehicle for autonomous surveying of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
summary: Autonomous ground vehicle surveying alpha/beta/gamma; radiation costmaps re-plan around contamination and experimentally reduce gamma dose to the robot.
relation: Dose-aware planning to protect the robot from a mapped field, but no hard cumulative budget, exit reserve or uncertain-source prediction.

title: A Novel Path Planning Approach for Mobile Robot in Radioactive Environment Based on Improved Deep Q Network Algorithm
summary: Improved dueling double DQN (ID3QN) for robot path planning in radioactive grid environments under path-length and accumulated-dose constraints, outperforming A*, GA, ACO and DQN variants.
relation: RL path planning minimizing accumulated dose in a known field, single agent; no search, budget or uncertainty.

title: Impact of gamma radiation on 8051 microcontroller performance
summary: Co-60 testing of a COTS AT89C51RD2 microcontroller to 1.5 kGy; it operated without failure or degradation up to about 0.6 kGy.
relation: Upper-range COTS MCU tolerance number for comparison with SBC (~111 Gy).

title: Modular Robots for Enabling Operations in Unstructured Extreme Environments
summary: Survey of robots for extreme environments; full text (Scholar Gateway) includes a figure of the total integrated dose of 23 nuclear robotic systems and their effective time before failure in Fukushima Daiichi Unit 2 (530 Gy/h), with humans (0.02 Gy) for comparison.
relation: Gives the per-robot TID and time-to-failure numbers that motivate a hard dose budget; no planning method.

title: Using Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection on a System-on-Chip under Gamma Radiation
summary: Uses ML anomaly detection on consumer FPGA/SoC measurements under gamma irradiation to anticipate total-ionizing-dose failure before the boards stop working.
relation: Evidence on cumulative TID failure of commodity electronics, supporting a hard per-robot dose budget.

title: Path planning in nuclear facility decommissioning: Research status, challenges, and opportunities
summary: Reviews radiation-aware path planning algorithms for decommissioning (grid, sampling, metaheuristic) and the decision factors involved.
relation: Survey of minimum-dose path planning; positions the thesis' dose-aware safety layer relative to this literature.

title: Gamma-Induced Image Degradation Analysis of Robot Vision Sensor for Autonomous Inspection of Nuclear Sites
summary: Examines CMOS camera degradation under gamma dose rates up to 3 Gy/min; radiation-induced noise makes images unreliable for visual odometry though still usable for surveillance.
relation: Shows perception degrades with dose rate before outright failure, relevant to sensing reliability in strong fields.

title: Metaheuristic minimum dose path planning for nuclear power plant decommissioning
summary: PSO and GA methods for minimum-dose paths of workers or robots during decommissioning; PSO beat grid- and sampling-based planners in cumulative dose and distance.
relation: Metaheuristic minimum-dose planning for workers/robots.

title: Path Planning for Nuclear Emergency Robot in Radiation Environment with Uneven Terrain
summary: Multi-layer costmap (radiation + traversability) with A* heuristic for an emergency robot that cannot pass areas of extremely high dose rate or steep slope.
relation: Treats a robot dose-rate limit as an impassable constraint (rate, not cumulative).

title: Use of Gaussian process regression for radiation mapping of a nuclear reactor with a mobile robot
summary: GPR with an MCNP6-benchmarked kernel interpolates sparse, noisy robot radiation measurements; demonstrated at the JSI TRIGA reactor hall.
relation: Probabilistic radiation-field estimate usable for predictive dose with uncertainty.

title: Simulating Ionising Radiation in Gazebo for Robotic Nuclear Inspection Challenges
summary: ROS/Gazebo plugin to simulate gamma sources and robot-mounted detectors in evolving nuclear environments, verified against MCNP6.
relation: Candidate simulation substrate for realistic robot dose/count rates; no planning or dose budget.

title: Vega—A small, low cost, ground robot for nuclear decommissioning
summary: Vega small ground robot for nuclear decommissioning; components irradiated to estimate operating lifetime in active environments; deployed at Dounreay.
relation: Source of empirical robot radiation tolerance/lifetime estimates to justify cumulative dose budgets.

title: The Use of Robots to Respond to Nuclear Accidents: Applying the Lessons of the Past to the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station
venue: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
summary: Reviews robots used at Three Mile Island, Chernobyl and Fukushima Daiichi and the lessons carried between accidents.
relation: Key review for the historical context of nuclear-accident robotics (TMI, Chernobyl, Fukushima).

title: Radiation Tolerance Testing Methodology of Robotic Manipulator Prior to Nuclear Waste Handling
summary: Presents a test methodology and results for a robotic arm with modern electronics operated at 10 Gy/h to simulate the harshest waste-handling facilities.
relation: Testing methodology for COTS robot tolerance.

title: An improved A* algorithm for searching the minimum dose path in nuclear facilities
summary: Improved A* algorithm for minimum-dose paths for nuclear plant workers in complex environments (Unity simulation).
relation: Representative grid-based minimum-dose path planner (A* with dose cost).

title: Evaluation and Analysis of Technologies for Robotic Platforms for the Nuclear Decommissioning
venue: International Conference on Design & Technology of Integrated Systems in Nanoscale Era
summary: Radiation hardness assurance procedure qualifying COTS electronics of a nuclear inspection robot to an initial TID target of 400 Gy.
relation: Gives a concrete robot TID tolerance figure usable to set dose budgets.

title: Allocation of Radiation Shielding Boards to Protect the Urban Search and Rescue Robots from Malfunctioning in the Radioactive Environments Arising from Decommissioning of the Nuclear Facility
summary: Allocates a finite budget of radiation shielding boards across a USAR UGV swarm to minimise absorbed doses and sensor malfunction, showing asymmetric allocation beats even allocation (competitive equilibrium, ILP).
relation: Treats robot dose protection as a team resource allocation problem with unequal shares, analogous to the thesis's unequal budgets; static allocation, no search or learning.

title: Robotic Development for the Nuclear Environment: Challenges and Strategy
summary: Reviews the challenges of deploying robots in nuclear environments, including radiation effects, remote maintenance and deployment constraints, and the nuclear industry's development/assessment processes.
relation: Background motivating per-robot radiation limits; no algorithms.

title: Radiation imaging using a compact Compton camera mounted on a crawler robot inside reactor buildings of Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station
venue: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology
summary: Deployed a compact Compton camera on a crawler robot in Unit 1 reactor building to visualise gamma-ray streaming and overlay it on a photogrammetric 3-D model.
relation: Real-world robot-based gamma imaging/source visualisation in a high-dose building.

title: Study of radiation effects in electronics of a hexapod robotic platform
summary: FLUKA study of damage rates in a PhantomX hexapod carrying a CZT detector and camera; notes high doses limit operational time and trades shielding against payload.
relation: Explicitly frames robot operating time as limited by dose; shielding vs capability trade-off.

title: Evaluation of 3D Printed Soft Robots in Radiation Environments and Comparison With Molded Counterparts
summary: PDMS soft robots lose mechanical performance with gamma dose but are minimally affected up to 20 kGy; an operating time of about 12 h is estimated for two of three nuclear radiation environments.
relation: Gives radiation tolerance evidence and an example of converting dose rate into a robot operating-time budget.

title: Irradiation test and hardness design for mobile rescue robot in nuclear environment
summary: Gamma irradiation tests of electronic modules of a mobile rescue robot with a 7-DOF arm, plus shielding/modular redeployment design and time-protection operational practices.
relation: Evidence on robot component radiation tolerance motivating a finite cumulative dose budget per robot.

title: A review of ground-based robotic systems for the characterization of nuclear environments
summary: Reviews ground robots for characterising nuclear environments from pre-TMI through Chernobyl to Fukushima Daiichi, highlighting constraints from extreme radiation, space and atmosphere.
relation: Key review for ground-robot radiation characterisation, the platform class used in the thesis.

title: Nuclear Radiation Degradation Study on HD Camera Based on CMOS Image Sensor at Different Dose Rates
summary: Co-60 irradiation of a COTS CMOS HD camera at 1-100 Gy/h; degradation worsens with dose rate, but the camera still worked at 10 Gy/h over 8 h (~80 Gy) with ~5 dB SNR loss.
relation: Camera tolerance data for robots in gamma fields.

title: Grid-based RRT* for minimum dose walking path-planning in complex radioactive environments
summary: GB-RRT* combines RRT* with grid search to find minimum-dose walking paths for workers in cluttered and narrow radioactive environments, outperforming RRT*.
relation: Sampling-based minimum-dose planning reference.

title: DL-RRT* algorithm for least dose path Re-planning in dynamic radioactive environments
summary: Combines RRT* and D* Lite for minimum-dose path re-planning when the radiation field changes.
relation: Dose-aware re-planning under changing fields, analogous to updating dose predictions online.

title: The path-planning in radioactive environment of nuclear facilities using an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm
summary: Title only: improved particle swarm optimization for path planning in radioactive environments of nuclear facilities.
relation: Classic dose-minimizing planning baseline in a known field.

title: Methods of minimising doses incurred by external exposure while moving in radiation hazardous areas
summary: Title only (no abstract): methods for minimising external-exposure dose while moving through radiation hazardous areas.
relation: Dose-minimizing movement in known fields, a precedent for dose-aware routing that the thesis extends to uncertain fields and robots.

title: Minimum dose method for walking-path planning of nuclear facilities
summary: Title only (no abstract): minimum dose method for walking-path planning in nuclear facilities.
relation: Classic dose-minimizing path precedent with known fields; the thesis faces uncertain fields and hard budgets.

title: Range-Finding Sensor Degradation in Gamma Radiation Environments
summary: Gamma testing of IR triangulation, sonar and laser rangefinders for nuclear remediation robots: IR sensitivity drifts with dose, the laser rangefinder fails abruptly at low dose, sonar degrades then fails; strong part-to-part variation.
relation: Evidence that failure dose is uncertain/variable, supporting a conservative budget with margin.

title: Emergency response by robots to Fukushima-Daiichi accident: summary and lessons learned
summary: Summarises robot deployments (Quince, JAEA-3, imported/donated unmanned machines) at Fukushima Daiichi and extracts organisational and system-level lessons.
relation: Background on real accident-response robot operations motivating autonomous, dose-aware robots.

title: Robotic control vehicle for measuring radiation in Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant
summary: Presents a shielded control vehicle with a gamma camera, TALON robot with radiation sensor and 3-D LIDAR for measuring hotspots (tens of mSv/h) at Fukushima Daiichi while cutting operator exposure to one third.
relation: Example of robot-based radiation survey in an accident site; human-exposure framing complements robot-dose budgeting.

title: Digital twins for robot-assisted nuclear decommissioning: a review of perception, radiological mapping, and model interoperability, with the DORADO project as a case study
summary: Review of digital twins for robot-assisted decommissioning covering radiological sensing, radiation-field estimation, mission planning and uncertainty propagation/V&V, with DORADO as case study; concludes end-to-end uncertainty management is a key barrier.
relation: Background on radiation-field estimation and uncertainty in robotic nuclear missions; supports the thesis' concern with estimate miscalibration.

title: Seeing the Invisible: Physics-Guided Visual Prompting for Temperature- and Radiation-Aware VLA Navigation
summary: PG-VP overlays physics-guided virtual obstacles so a frozen VLA navigation policy avoids invisible radiation or thermal hazards.
relation: Radiation-aware navigation by hazard masking; no budget or search.

title: Radiation Hardened LIDAR Sensor: Conceptual Design, Testing, and Performance Evaluation
summary: Notes standard silicon LIDARs fail quickly in gamma fields and designs a LIDAR prototype from components expected to tolerate up to 1 MGy.
relation: Rad-hard alternative illustrating the gap between COTS (~100 Gy) and hardened (~MGy) tolerance.

title: An Improved Prototypical Network–based Method for Diagnosing Gamma Radiation Faults in Optical Encoders
summary: Prototypical-network method to diagnose gamma-radiation-induced faults in optical encoder circuits of nuclear robots from few samples.
relation: Evidence of radiation-induced robot sensor failures; diagnostic, not planning.

title: Development and Application of Robotics for Decommissioning of Fukushima Daiichi NPS by IRID
summary: Reports IRID's robots for investigating primary containment vessels at Fukushima Daiichi to locate fuel debris, tailored to each unit's accident scenario.
relation: Background on current decommissioning robots operating in extreme gamma fields.

title: Optimal path planning in a real-world radioactive environment: A comparative study of A-star and Dijkstra algorithms
summary: Compares A* and Dijkstra for optimal low-dose paths in a real-world radioactive environment.
relation: Benchmark comparison of graph planners with dose cost.

title: Arduino programming of an educational robotic platform applied in radiological accident simulation
summary: Arduino six-wheel robot with RadEye detector for radiological accident simulation; radiation field caused interference in control signals, shielding of boards recommended.
relation: Anecdotal evidence that radiation degrades robot electronics/communication, motivating robot dose limits.

title: Research on the degradation of resolution in cameras based on CMOS image sensor under γ- and X-rays irradiation
venue: Radiation effects and defects in solids (Print)
summary: Irradiation of CMOS image sensors with Co-60 gamma and X-rays shows TID-driven degradation of dark current, full well capacity and camera resolution.
relation: Component-level evidence of Co-60 TID damage to robot cameras, informing per-robot dose budgets.

title: Applicability of an Ionising Radiation Measuring System for Real-Time Effective-Dose-Optimised Route Finding Solution during Nuclear Accidents
summary: Real-time measurement system that estimates effective dose of candidate routes for rescue vehicles through contaminated nuclear-accident areas, accounting for vehicle shielding, speed and travel time.
relation: Dose-optimal route selection precedent, but for crewed vehicles/evacuees from measured fields, not robots with a hard budget and an uncertain source estimate.

title: Degradation Mechanism of Piezoresistive Sensors Under the Influence of γ -Ray Irradiation
summary: Gamma irradiation of MEMS piezoresistive pressure sensors up to 27.9 Mrad: sensitivity changed <0.8% but bridge offset drifted 139%.
relation: Provides component cumulative-dose degradation numbers relevant to robot dose budgets.

title: Detailed visualization of radioactive hotspots inside the unit 1 reactor building of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station using an integrated Radiation Imaging System mounted on a Mecanum wheel robot
venue: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology
summary: Mecanum-wheel robot with Compton camera, SLAM and survey meter visualised radioactive hotspots and dose-rate distribution inside Fukushima Daiichi Unit 1.
relation: Real deployment evidence for robot radiation characterisation in high-dose buildings; no autonomy or dose budget.

title: Effect of ionising radiation on the mechanical and structural properties of 3D printed plastics
summary: Tensile and structural properties of FFF printed polymers after gamma doses up to 5.3 MGy; Nylon most robust, PLA most sensitive.
relation: Material dose-tolerance data relevant to robot structural parts; much higher doses than electronics limits.

title: Minimum collective dose based optimal evacuation path-planning method under nuclear accidents
summary: Accumulated-dose Dijkstra plus equilibrium model to plan minimum collective dose evacuation routes after a nuclear accident.
relation: Exit planning minimizing dose for humans in a known field; analogous to robots' exit path cost.

title: An Optimization Algorithm Based on Artificial Potential Field and Particle Swarm Optimization to Avoid Radiation Exposure Under Radioactive Environment
summary: APF tuned by PSO generates radiation-avoiding trajectories for personnel among known sources.
relation: Dose-avoiding path planning with known sources; baseline-level related work.

title: The effects of Total Ionizing Dose irradiation on supercapacitors deployed in nuclear decommissioning environments
summary: 100 F supercapacitors irradiated with Co-60 showed negligible capacitance change up to 40 kGy and unchanged internal resistance/self-discharge up to 89 kGy.
relation: Provides component-level TID tolerance numbers useful for setting plausible robot dose budgets.

title: Total-Ionizing-Dose Effects, Border Traps, and 1/f Noise in Emerging MOS Technologies
summary: Reviews TID effects in emerging MOS technologies; failure doses often 100 krad to 1 Mrad(SiO2) or higher.
relation: Source for electronics failure-dose numbers that set robot dose budgets.

title: Probabilistic roadmap method for path-planning in radioactive environment of nuclear facilities
summary: PRM-based path planning that minimises dose in radioactive environments of nuclear facilities (title-based; no abstract returned).
relation: Roadmap-based dose-aware planning reference.

title: A Robot to Monitor Nuclear Facilities: Using Autonomous Radiation-Monitoring Assistance to Reduce Risk and Cost
summary: Argues for autonomous radiation-monitoring robots in nuclear facilities to replace human operators and reduce risk and cost.
relation: Motivational precedent for robotic radiation monitoring; no dose budget or source search.

title: A sampling-based method with virtual reality technology to provide minimum dose path navigation for occupational workers in nuclear facilities
summary: Title only: sampling-based minimum dose path navigation for workers in nuclear facilities with VR.
relation: Dose-minimizing path planning precedent in known fields.

title: Impact of Cobalt-60 Gamma Radiation Source on Electronic Devices using Geant4
summary: Geant4 simulation and Geiger-Muller measurements of an Atmega328 exposed to a Co-60 source at varying distances, discussed via the inverse-square law.
relation: Evidence on Co-60 effects on robot-grade electronics; minor support for the dose-budget motivation.

title: Dynamic minimum dose path-searching method for virtual nuclear facilities
summary: Dynamic minimum-dose path search for workers in virtual nuclear facilities.
relation: Early minimum-dose path method.

title: Robots in the nuclear industry: a review of technologies and applications
summary: Reviews robot use in the nuclear power industry for test/inspection and decommissioning, with product examples and case histories.
relation: General review background for nuclear robotics.

title: Practical design of robots operating in radiation environments
summary: Proposes a modular, hierarchical electrical circuit architecture so robot components can withstand radiation without the cost and limited functionality of dedicated rad-hard parts.
relation: Background on hardening by architecture.

title: The Use of Robotics and Automation in Nuclear Decommissioning
summary: Reviews the scope for robotics and automation in nuclear decommissioning to speed demolition and reduce worker exposure.
relation: Early decommissioning-robotics background.

title: Energy-Aware Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization with Depletion Safety Constraints for Multi-Robot Coordination
summary: EA-MAPPO adds energy-augmented observations and shaped rewards; SEA-MAPPO adds predictive action masking (learned energy predictor, R2=0.89) to avoid battery depletion, validated on the Robotarium and physical GTernal robots with zero depletion events.
relation: Closest architectural analogue: MAPPO + learned per-robot consumption predictor + predictive action mask on a non-renewable resource; differs in that energy cost is not tied to an uncertain belief over a hazard source and no chance-constraint target is set.

title: Who Bears the Burden? Learning Responsibility for Shared Constraints in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: LiRA learns each agent's share of a common Lagrange multiplier for a shared cost budget, optimizing social welfare; tested with 3-400 agents.
relation: Directly relevant to risk sharing: how a team constraint's burden is allocated across agents; the thesis uses individual dose budgets, possibly unequal.

title: From Cumulative Constraints to Adaptive Runtime Safety Control for Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning
summary: CPSS tracks the remaining cumulative safety budget, projects it into a time-varying admissible risk threshold and filters actions whose predicted cost exceeds it, with cumulative cost bounds.
relation: Very close mechanism to the thesis' budget-aware safety layer, but single-agent driving without exit reserve or estimate-dependent cost.

title: Safe multi-agent reinforcement learning for multi-robot control
summary: Formulates safe MARL as a constrained Markov game with per-agent constraints and proposes MACPO and MAPPO-Lagrangian, plus Safe MAMuJoCo/MARobosuite/MAIG benchmarks.
relation: Source of the MAPPO-Lagrangian baseline used in the thesis; per-robot constraints in expectation, which the thesis contrasts with its mission-level chance constraint.

title: Provably Safe Reinforcement Learning: Conceptual Analysis, Survey, and Benchmarking
summary: Categorizes provably safe RL into action replacement, projection and masking, benchmarks them, and finds that adding a penalty when the safety verifier intervenes improves training.
relation: Taxonomy that places the thesis' dose mask (masking) and withdraw action (replacement); supports adding an intervention penalty.

title: SAUTE RL: Almost Surely Safe Reinforcement Learning Using State Augmentation
summary: Augments the state with the remaining safety budget and reshapes the objective so that constraints are satisfied almost surely; plug-and-play with any RL algorithm.
relation: Formal basis for feeding remaining dose budget into the robot observation and for treating budget exhaustion as terminal.

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration
summary: Simmer: augments state with a safety state whose initial value is the safety budget and schedules that budget during training, improving safety and stabilizing Lagrangian training.
relation: Suggests budget curricula as an alternative remedy to MAPPO-L timidity.

title: Model-Based Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning via Separated Proportional-Integral Lagrangian
